beats.care: A good example of earning from nature without destroying it. NITI Aayog has highlighted it.
beats.what: 286 Kolam, Gond and Lambada families in Narnoor mandal earned ₹3,500 to ₹8,000 each from lac in the first harvest.
beats.why: Lac is a resin made by insects on trees. Harvesting it doesn't need trees to be cut, and the district plans to expand to 20 villages.

cards.body: In Khairdatwa village, 12 tribal women run a Mahua laddu unit set up with government support. The laddus may go to Ashram schools and Anganwadis.
Pendur Laxman of Sungapur, over several cycles.

cards.body: Lac is used in bangles, varnish, food glaze and even medicine coatings.

cards.q: Would you buy forest products made by tribal groups?

cards.why: Lac is a resin secreted by lac insects living on host trees like Palash.

hook: Tribal families in Adilabad earn from trees *without cutting them*

learn.t: Jharkhand is India's biggest lac producer, which is why trainers came from there.

sources.name: The Hindu
sources.title: Tribals find new sources of income from forests (print, Hyderabad edition, 24 Oct, p.4)

tldr: Families in Adilabad are earning extra from lac grown on Palash trees, and women are making laddus from Mahua flowers.
